column1: How do you use bat as a previewer for other tools?
column2: With fzf: fzf --preview 'bat --color=always {}'. With git: git diff | bat -l diff. As pager: export BAT_PAGER='less -RF'. bat -A shows whitespace characters (tabs, spaces, newlines).

column1: When do you still use classic tools (grep, find, cat) over modern ones?
column2: On remote servers without modern tools installed. In shell scripts that must be portable. In Dockerfiles (minimize image size). When piping to other programs that expect standard output format. Know both — modern for interactive work, classic for portability.

column1: You need to find all YAML files containing 'replicas' in a monorepo. Which tool chain do you pick?
column2: rg 'replicas' -t yaml for the answer. If you need to browse the results interactively: rg 'replicas' -t yaml -l | fzf --preview 'bat --color=always {}'. Classic equivalent takes 3+ commands; rg does it in one.

column1: How do you use jq to triage JSON logs from an application?
column2: cat app.log | jq 'select(.level == \error\")' (filter errors). Count by service: jq -r 'select(.level == \"error\") | .service' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn. Table output: jq -r '[.timestamp, .service, .message] | @tsv' | column -t"

column1: What is the modern-tool equivalent of 'find . -name *.yaml | xargs grep replicas | sort'?
column2: rg 'replicas' -t yaml. One command replaces the entire pipeline. Add -C 2 for context, -l for file names only, --stats for totals. rg handles .gitignore, binary files, and multi-threading automatically.

column1: How do you find and execute a command on matching files with fd?
column2: fd -e py -x wc -l (count lines in each Python file). fd -e log -X rm (delete all .log files — -X batches into one command, -x runs per file). Add -H to include hidden files.

column1: What is fzf and what problem does it solve?
column2: fzf is an interactive fuzzy finder. Turns any list into a searchable, selectable menu. Pipe anything into it: kubectl get pods | fzf, git branch | fzf, history | fzf. Transforms CLI workflows from recall-based to recognition-based.

column1: How do you filter and reshape JSON with jq?
column2: Filter: jq '.items[] | select(.status == \running\")'. Reshape: jq '{name: .metadata.name, phase: .status.phase}'. Raw output: jq -r '.name' (no quotes). Slurp: jq -s '.' (read all inputs into array)."

column1: How do you search only specific file types with rg?
column2: rg 'pattern' -t yaml (built-in type filter). rg 'pattern' -g '*.yaml' (glob filter). rg -t py -g '!test*' 'pattern' (Python files excluding tests). rg --type-list shows all built-in types.

column1: What does zoxide replace and how does it learn?
column2: zoxide replaces cd. It learns from your navigation — tracks directory frequency and recency (frecency). z exercises jumps to most-visited match. zi opens interactive selection with fzf. Setup: eval \$(zoxide init bash)\""
